summary: Drafted 1st overall by the Raiders (2025 Heisman winner, Indiana) specifically so Las Vegas could move on from Geno Smith, who was traded to the Jets. Entered camp as the presumptive Week 1 starter as a true rookie — no NFL stat history exists to project him from.

Traded from Las Vegas to the Jets (late-round pick swap) after the Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza 1st overall. Smith takes over as Jets starter — a fresh offensive context after a rough 2025 (league-high 17 INTs, 55 sacks taken behind a poor Raiders line).

Traded from the Jets to Kansas City as Patrick Mahomes' backup while Mahomes recovers from a torn ACL/LCL. Andy Reid calls Fields a "legitimate starting quarterback" who could open games if Mahomes isn't ready, though Mahomes has reportedly progressed quickly and could reclaim the job early. Fields is also fending off a camp push from 7th-round rookie Garrett Nussmeier.

Lions hired Drew Petzing (ex-Cardinals) as offensive coordinator for 2026. Goff says the offense is being built around Detroit's current personnel, with more bootlegs/rollouts and a slightly expanded pre-snap role for Goff at the line — last season's play-calling tendencies don't automatically carry forward.

Entering Year 2 under HC Ben Johnson (his second full offseason together). Camp reviews are mixed — "up and down," unremarkable preseason debut — but Johnson says nothing has been alarming and points to real anticipation/red-zone progress. Johnson is also floating more shotgun usage, an evolution from last year's install.

Battling for the Saints' backup job behind confirmed 2026 starter Tyler Shough (per the existing team-scoped note on file), not competing for the top job himself. Preseason showing has been underwhelming (8/11, 42 yards, 3.8 YPA in his start vs. Jacksonville) — no clear path to snaps unless Shough is hurt.

Unquestioned Giants starter entering 2026 after winning the job from Russell Wilson midway through his 2025 rookie season (2,200 yards, 15 TD, 5 INT passing plus 9 rushing TDs). Enters Year 2 with a deeper receiving room — new TE Isaiah Likely and 3rd-round WR Malachi Fields — and a new starting LT (Francis Mauigoa).

Says he's "pretty much past" the throwing-wrist ligament injury that required surgery; threw for 4,000 yards and 39 TDs in his return season. No lingering camp limitation reported. Bengals also added defensive reinforcements (Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe, Bryan Cook, Kyle Dugger) this offseason, which doesn't change his workload but signals the team building around him rather than a rebuild.

Fully healthy after a 2025 marred by knee, hamstring, and a severe dislocated elbow (missed 10 games total). GM Adam Peters says he's "in great shape" and camp/joint-practice reps have shown no mobility limitations. Team is being cautious with his preseason snap count as a precaution, not a lingering issue.

Panthers are deliberately NOT extending him before the season — GM Dan Morgan wants to see 2026 play out (including a tough early slate vs. PHI/SEA/GB/BAL) before committing. Described as one of the highest-stakes "prove it" years at QB league-wide; a strong season pays him well, a poor one puts his Carolina future in doubt.

Confirmed at camp "zero debate" that 2026 is his final season. Steelers hired Mike McCarthy (his longtime Green Bay HC) this offseason, which Rodgers said factored into his decision to play one more year. No injury/performance concerns reported — this is a career-timeline note, not a health one.

No contract extension has materialized despite the Seahawks having two years left on his deal — Seattle's stated policy is to not extend players with multiple years remaining. Playing into 2026 without long-term security is a real incentive dynamic, though there's no reported change to his starting role.

Named the Cardinals' 2026 starter after Kyler Murray suffered a season-ending Lisfranc/foot injury in 2025 (Brissett went 1st in the NFL in passing yards from Week 6 on) and Arizona chose not to bring Murray back — Murray signed with Minnesota and won the Vikings' 2026 starting job over J.J. McCarthy (see separate note). Brissett, 33, isn't viewed as a long-term answer but is the clear 2026 QB1.

Lost the Vikings' 2026 starting job to free-agent-signed Kyler Murray after an open training camp competition (HC Kevin O'Connell named Murray the starter Aug. 11) — this supersedes any earlier-August note assuming McCarthy was the incumbent starter. McCarthy opens the season as backup after a 10-start rookie 2025 that ended with a torn meniscus.

Eagles fired OC Kevin Patullo after a 2025 offensive regression (7th to 19th in scoring, 8th to 24th in yards) and promoted Sean Mannion to play-caller — Hurts' 7th different play-caller in 7 NFL seasons. A real scheme-continuity risk after Philadelphia's offense visibly declined without Kellen Moore (who left to be Saints HC).

Added Jaylen Waddle as a new deep-threat weapon (some missed camp time with minor injuries but flashed explosiveness), while rookie Pat Bryant "ran away with" the job of Nix's most trusted target through camp. Courtland Sutton remains involved but was load-managed rather than a full-camp participant. Materially different receiving corps than his 2025 tape reflects.

Re-signed as Colts starter (March 2026) despite a torn Achilles suffered in early December 2025 — the team is leaning on him anyway as its best 2026 option. Anthony Richardson, once the presumed future starter, is now fighting Riley Leonard for the No. 2 job behind Jones after requesting (and being denied) a trade.

Fully healthy entering 2026 (unlike a hampered 2025) after Houston overhauled its offensive line and culture; new RB David Montgomery (via trade from Detroit) joins the backfield, and the Stroud–Jayden Higgins connection is described as sharpening through camp. A meaningfully upgraded supporting cast versus last season.

Avoided offseason back surgery (aggravated disc managed non-surgically) and played all 17 games in 2025, his first full slate since 2021 — a positive durability signal heading into the second year of his two-year deal, though his age/injury history remains a real risk to monitor.

No notable injury or role news out of camp — fully healthy and sharp in practice reports, with the only change being new HC/OC-driven scheme installation under Jim Harbaugh's second full offseason. Included for completeness since last season's per-game rate is a reasonable baseline as-is.
